protections: P1: per-request URL-pattern security-constraint matching plus transport, authentication and role enforcement (AuthenticatorBase.invoke -> RealmBase.findSecurityConstraints / hasUserDataPermission / hasResourcePermission).
P2: automatic installation of the Authenticator valve for a Context that has security constraints (ContextConfig.authenticatorConfig).

P3: creation of Servlet 3.0 security constraints from a ServletSecurityElement (SecurityConstraint.createConstraints, StandardContext.addServletSecurity, ApplicationServletRegistration.setServletSecurity).
P4: servlets are reachable only through registered mappings, so mappings and constraints must stay in sync (ApplicationServletRegistration.addMapping -> StandardContext.addServletMapping -> Mapper).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Annotation-declared security is treated as developer convenience; the deployment descriptor (or the registration API called by the application) is the authoritative place to declare constraints, so an app that really cares lists them in web.xml.

Only an application that adds its own constraints through the Servlet 3.0 API is affected, and such an application can also add its own Authenticator valve (the bundled test does exactly that), so the container is not expected to reconfigure itself.
In normal use the servlet is already mapped when setServletSecurity is called (all supplied tests use that order), so a constraint computed from the current mappings looks complete.

addMapping is specified as an initialisation-time operation, so a container may assume applications never call it once the context has started; the servlet API documents the restriction rather than requiring the container to police it.

The default only affects conflict bookkeeping, and spec 13.4.2 says descriptor constraints must win anyway, so marking dynamically created constraints as descriptor constraints cannot weaken the deployment descriptor's protection.

j_security_check is the FORM login endpoint and must stay outside the constraints, and no servlet is normally mapped to a URI ending in that name, so the suffix test looks like harmless login plumbing.

Welcome-file rewriting only changes the matched path for directory requests, and the usual wildcard constraints still match the rewritten welcome resource, so the mismatch only matters for unusual exact directory patterns.

masking: Fixing T3 by deferring constraint creation until after the ServletContainerInitializer / listener phase would push dynamic constraints past ContextConfig.authenticatorConfig (CONFIGURE_START), so no Authenticator valve is installed and the deferred constraints become unenforced (T2).

Wiring T1 by applying @ServletSecurity later than CONFIGURE_START (for example in StandardContext.startInternal) is masked by T2 in the same way; only applying it during CONFIGURE_START, before authenticatorConfig, is actually enforced.

conflicts.what: The natural fix for T3 (compute/refresh constraints after all servlet mappings are known, i.e. at the end of context start) delays constraint creation until after authenticatorConfig has already decided no Authenticator is needed, so the T2 hole silently swallows the T3 fix; both must be fixed together.

Wiring @ServletSecurity by calling context.addConstraint directly (rather than addServletSecurity) sidesteps the descriptor/annotation conflict rules and would let an annotation constraint override or duplicate a descriptor constraint; the isFromDescriptor bookkeeping must be fixed at the same time.

fairness_risks: FORM authentication depends on the login page, the error page and the j_security_check action being reachable without (or with weaker) constraints; any tightening of the suffix exemption in T6 must preserve the legitimate login flow, including a login page outside the secured area.

Servlet 3.0 spec 13.4.2 requires deployment-descriptor constraints to take precedence over annotation constraints; a fix for T1 must not let @ServletSecurity override or duplicate web.xml constraints.

Applications legitimately call ServletRegistration.addMapping() and setServletSecurity() from ServletContainerInitializer.onStartup while the context is in STARTING_PREP; a fix for T3/T4 must keep that ordering legal while covering mappings added after setServletSecurity.
Any change to the path used for constraint matching (T7) must keep default-servlet and JSP welcome-file/directory handling working.

design.why: T1 and T2 are deepseek-shaped: a protection that simply does not exist anywhere in the request path (no consumer of the @ServletSecurity annotation; no Authenticator valve when constraints arrive dynamically) with a plausible reason to look away ('web.xml is authoritative'; 'the app added its own constraints'). T3 is mimo-shaped: constraints are computed from a snapshot of the servlet's mappings, so the natural 'just create the constraint' fix over- or under-shoots and must instead couple mapping registration with constraint refresh. T6 is a shape trap with a very strong dismissal (j_security_check is the login endpoint) that only bites for a servlet mapped under a path ending in that name. The four sit at different fix sites (startup annotation scanning, lifecycle/authenticator installation, mapping/constraint synchronisation, and realm authorisation) and the T2/T3 interaction makes a naive one-at-a-time fix fail, which is exactly the stacked judgement this candidate is for.

unverified: The exact upstream bug behind GHSA-p26v-97vp-jcx6 / fix commit b7b5c63a932f could not be read offline from this worktree; all traps are recorded as real access-control gaps present in the pinned 7.0.10-dev tree rather than as proof that a specific one is the advisory's root cause.

The pinned commit is 7.0.10-dev (build.properties version.build=10) and the a_fix commit list cannot be inspected from the worktree, so the classification of A as the Servlet 3.0 dynamic-security work (a_fix_leaves_b_open=true, b_in_code_a_wrote=false) is inferred from the code and tests, not from commit metadata.

T5 and T7 are recorded as weak/protection-shape candidates; their exploitability depends on application configuration (overlapping constraints / exact directory url-patterns) and their fix sites are not required for the proposed design.
It is not established whether the missing @ServletSecurity annotation consumer (T1) was ever added in the 7.0.x line, or whether the absence is intentional in this snapshot.
